decisions.title: Feet at last
decisions.situation: You pull off one sock. There was a foot in there the whole time. The other sock now looks suspicious.

choices.label: Free the other foot
Try putting the sock back
Wave the sock around

result.title: Matching feet
result.body: Two socks off. Ten toes accounted for. You start wiggling them.

journal.text: I pulled off both socks and investigated my toes.

decisions.title: Permanent exhibition
decisions.situation: You draw a huge purple person on the wall. Alice walks in while you are adding the teeth.

choices.label: Show off your work
Help clean it up
Blame a very tall baby

result.title: Mixed reviews
result.body: Alice gives you paper. The wall gets a long scrub.

journal.text: I drew a purple person on the wall. It was not a commissioned piece.

decisions.title: Customer complaint
decisions.situation: Alice takes you for a haircut. You are convinced the cape means you have been promoted to wizard.

choices.label: Cast a spell on the comb
Ask what every tool does
Ask Alice to hold your hand

result.title: Comb survives
result.body: The comb refuses to turn into a frog. Your haircut carries on.

journal.text: I tried magic during a haircut. It did not affect the comb.

decisions.title: Something under the blanket
decisions.situation: You tell Alice there is a dragon under your blanket. Alice asks whether it would like a bedtime story.

choices.label: Make room for one more listener
Invent the dragon’s entire biography
Ask Alice to check properly

result.title: A civilised dragon
result.body: The dragon listens very quietly. Alice does all the voices.

journal.text: My imaginary dragon joined bedtime stories.

decisions.title: The museum has escaped
decisions.situation: You empty your pocket collection onto the table for Alice. Three stones. A leaf. A slug you thought was another leaf. The slug makes for the edge.

choices.label: Give Alice the guided tour
Return the slug before it reaches the floor
Claim the slug lives here now

result.title: Please follow the shiny line
result.body: You describe the stones while Alice catches the slug on a leaf. Your only moving exhibit is removed halfway through the tour.

journal.text: I gave Alice a museum tour while a slug escaped from my pocket collection.

decisions.title: Birthday invitation
decisions.situation: Miguel invites you to a birthday party at an arcade. The invitation has more glitter than useful information.

choices.label: Ask Alice for permission
Ask Miguel for more details
Politely decline

result.title: Adults need an address
result.body: Alice checks the time and supervision. Their answer and any plan are recorded below. Nothing is paid just for asking.

journal.text: I asked Alice for permission to go to Miguel’s arcade birthday.

decisions.title: Party day
decisions.situation: Miguel’s arcade birthday is here. Alice agreed to take you. The quoted outing costs R$ 15,00, paid by Alice only if you go.

choices.label: Go with Alice · R$ 15,00
Stay home · no charge

result.title: High score, low dignity
result.body: You and Miguel take turns at the machines. Alice pays the quoted outing cost. Nobody wins enough tickets to retire.

journal.text: I went to Miguel’s arcade birthday with Alice.

decisions.title: The handle is no longer involved
decisions.situation: You knock Alice’s favourite mug off the table. The handle leaves the rest of the mug. Nobody saw.

choices.label: Tell Alice what happened
Offer to help repair it
Slide the evidence behind a plant

result.title: Bad news, delivered properly
result.body: Alice is disappointed about the mug and pleased you said something.

journal.text: I admitted breaking Alice’s mug.

decisions.title: Unlimited dragons, limited shelf space
decisions.situation: At the library, you find a book so big you need both arms to carry it. The return desk suddenly looks very far away.

choices.label: Commit to the enormous book
Find a smaller story you love
Ask the librarian for a recommendation

result.title: An ambitious loan
result.body: You finish some of it, skip a confusing chapter, and learn three words you immediately misuse.

journal.text: I borrowed the largest book I could carry.

decisions.title: Your name on the cover
decisions.situation: Miguel asks you to share a class project. Laura has given you two months. That sounds like a problem for Future You.

choices.label: Promise to write your section
Ask to work separately
Admit you cannot commit

result.title: Future You has been notified
result.body: You agree on a section to write. The deadline is saved; agreeing has not completed any work.

journal.text: I agreed to write a section of a class project with Miguel.

decisions.title: The project is due
decisions.situation: Miguel is putting the class project together. Laura wants your section today. The blank page has enjoyed two months of peace.

choices.label: Finish your section
Ask Laura for help
Leave your section blank

result.title: Your name belongs on it
result.body: You finish your section and explain it to Miguel. Laura records the work you actually did.

journal.text: I finished my section of the class project with Miguel.

decisions.title: A very loud rehearsal
decisions.situation: The school alarm sounds during a practice evacuation. Laura asks everyone to leave calmly. Your chair has other ideas about moving quietly.

choices.label: Follow the instructions and leave your things
Ask Laura where to go
Delay to pack everything neatly

result.title: All accounted for
result.body: Laura checks the class at the meeting point. Your bag can wait inside.

journal.text: I followed Laura’s instructions during a practice evacuation.

decisions.title: Your parent knows this level
decisions.situation: You promise Alice one last round. They sit down, watch your first attempt and say, “I used to beat this blindfolded.” This is an outrageous development.

choices.label: Stop before they can demonstrate
Agree on one round each, then stop
Demand rematches until you win

result.title: Dignity preserved
result.body: You keep your promise and turn it off. Alice seems more pleased about that than any old high score.

journal.text: I stopped a game when I had promised Alice I would.

decisions.title: A promise remembered
decisions.situation: Two years after that class project, Miguel Silva brings it up. Back then, you finished your section.

choices.label: Remember doing your part
Tell Miguel it does not matter
Leave it in the past

result.title: An old project, an honest conversation
result.body: You acknowledge that you finished your section. Miguel hears you out.

journal.text: I talked honestly with Miguel about our old project, when I finished my section.

decisions.title: The microphone is still on
decisions.situation: After a class announcement, Miguel whispers that the school jingle sounds like a microwave. The microphone is still on.

choices.label: Switch it off and warn them
Help make a short apology
Add microwave sound effects

result.title: Broadcast ends
result.body: Most people heard the first comment. You prevent a second one.

journal.text: I switched off a live microphone before Miguel said anything worse.

decisions.title: Forwarded with absolutely no evidence
decisions.situation: A group chat is circulating an embarrassing rumour about someone your age. The source appears to be “everyone knows”.

choices.label: Ask whether anyone actually knows
Mute it and step away
Forward it for a reaction

result.title: An inconvenient question
result.body: Nobody produces evidence. The conversation changes topic with suspicious speed.

journal.text: I challenged a rumour in a group chat.

decisions.title: Sent to the group
decisions.situation: You send “Whoever made this group is unbearable” to the group itself. The admin replies, “Hi.” You can see several people typing.

choices.label: Mute the group and disappear
Admit you meant a different chat
Explain that autocorrect meant “adorable”

result.title: A successful retreat
result.body: You miss the replies and spend the afternoon doing something else. The message remains embarrassing; you stop watching it happen.

journal.text: I muted a group after sending an insulting message to it.

decisions.title: The cake has a message
decisions.situation: Miguel made a cake iced with an insult about Laura. It was meant for a private joke. Laura has just asked what is in the box.

choices.label: Eat the incriminating slice immediately
Tell Laura what the cake says
Open the box and offer them a slice

result.title: The evidence was mostly icing
result.body: You stuff the message into your mouth. Laura asks a second question, which you cannot answer. Miguel struggles not to laugh.

journal.text: I ate a slice of Miguel’s cake to hide its insulting message.

decisions.title: Your debut single is chemistry
decisions.situation: Miguel secretly records you singing chemistry definitions and adds a dance beat. The file is called “Desperate for Zinc”. They want to send it to the class.

choices.label: Make them delete the recording
Demand credit as the anonymous vocalist
Record a completely unnecessary key change

result.title: An extremely limited release
result.body: Miguel deletes it while you watch. They call you difficult. You call them a record label with no permission forms.

journal.text: I made Miguel delete a secret recording of my chemistry revision song.

decisions.title: Your murderous past
decisions.situation: A walking-tour guide points straight at you and tells the group you are the ghost of a notorious murderer. You are outside a shop in Rio de Janeiro, holding a sandwich.

choices.label: Explain that you are alive and eating lunch
Ask what crimes you supposedly committed
Follow the tour without breaking eye contact

result.title: New evidence
result.body: The guide calls your sandwich an unsettling detail. You take a large bite. A tourist asks whether ghosts can eat cheese. The guide moves the group along.

journal.text: I corrected a walking tour that mistook me for a murderer’s ghost in Rio de Janeiro.

decisions.title: You need medical attention
decisions.situation: Your symptoms have become serious: unusual thirst and persistent fatigue. A hospital assessment can begin treatment and may require a short stay. The quoted care costs R$0.00; an unpaid emergency bill remains a real obligation.

choices.label: Accept hospital assessment
Decline assessment

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

decisions.title: You must make the most of it
decisions.situation: You feel better rested than usual and immediately begin planning enough tasks to use every available bit of energy.

choices.label: Choose a few priorities and leave room
Enjoy feeling well without a quota
Fill every bit of the day

result.title: A useful day with an ending
result.body: You use some energy without treating all of it as a resource that must be exhausted.

journal.text: I paced a good day instead of filling every available moment.

decisions.title: The door does not believe in you
decisions.situation: An automatic shop door refuses to open for you. It opens for a child, a trolley and a blowing receipt. You step forward. Nothing. The cashier points at the sensor and suggests waving.

choices.label: Ask the cashier to let you out
Follow the trolley out
Perform an increasingly furious dance

result.title: Assisted departure
result.body: The cashier walks over. The doors open immediately for them. They hold the sensor while you leave, like a bouncer escorting out a ghost.

journal.text: I had to ask a cashier to release me through an automatic door.

decisions.title: One more attempt at your name
decisions.situation: At a local discussion group, the host mispronounces your name twice and then suggests a nickname you have never used.

choices.label: Say your name clearly once more
Turn the correction into a light joke
Use the nickname for the afternoon

result.title: A manageable correction
result.body: The host repeats it correctly and moves on. The proposed nickname retires before its first appearance.

journal.text: I corrected my name instead of accepting an unwanted nickname.

decisions.title: The naked gardener
decisions.situation: The community garden in Rio de Janeiro needs volunteers. Its organiser is wearing a novelty apron printed with a naked torso and refuses to explain it.

choices.label: Weed beside the alarming apron
Ask about the plants, very specifically
Decide you have seen enough nature

result.title: A productive misunderstanding
result.body: You clear a whole bed. Three passers-by stop to stare before realising the torso has pockets.

journal.text: I volunteered beside a gardener in an alarming novelty apron in Rio de Janeiro.

decisions.title: The sofa is judging you
decisions.situation: Autoplay follows your programme with a competitive fitness class. A man who appears to have been assembled entirely from elbows challenges you to beat your personal best.

choices.label: Switch to the beginner version and try it
Invent a chair-based version
Keep up with him at full speed

result.title: An achievable number of elbows
result.body: You complete the gentler routine. The instructor says anyone can do it, then folds himself into a shape you decline to investigate.

journal.text: I followed a beginner workout after a fitness video appeared on autoplay.

decisions.title: The compliment has the wrong address
decisions.situation: Someone praises an anonymous poem you were standing beside at a free exhibition. You did not write it. They are waiting for you to explain its “raw emotional honesty”.

choices.label: Thank them, then admit it is not yours
Point out the actual poet’s name
Accept the praise and invent your inspiration

result.title: A narrow escape from poetry
result.body: They laugh at the mix-up. You both admit you were not entirely sure what the last line meant.

journal.text: I corrected a stranger who thought I had written a poem.

decisions.title: You said that part out loud
decisions.situation: You rehearse a devastating comeback while walking. A stranger turns around just as you announce, “That is why nobody trusts your ferret.”

choices.label: Explain that you were arguing in your head
Write the useful point down privately
Pretend to be on an important phone call

result.title: No actual ferret dispute
result.body: The stranger accepts the explanation and walks on a little faster. You retire the argument before it recruits anyone else.

journal.text: I stopped an imaginary argument after saying part of it aloud.

decisions.title: Not the tabletop version
decisions.situation: At a craft workshop, you pull the tab on a kit labelled “decorative boat”. A full-size inflatable canoe starts filling the room. The tiny instruction sheet says to inflate outdoors.

choices.label: Deflate it before it reaches the doorway
Climb in and ask for paddles
Insist the picture on the box was misleading

result.title: A long public fart
result.body: You open the valve. The canoe collapses over eight uninterrupted seconds of rude noise. The instructor waits until everyone has stopped laughing to explain the warning.

journal.text: I deflated a full-size canoe during a crowded craft workshop.

decisions.title: Honest feedback, preferably positive
decisions.situation: At a free tasting, you try a cracker that tastes strongly of cupboard. The demonstrator asks for a glowing testimonial while holding a camera.

choices.label: Suggest improving the flavour first
Praise how neatly it broke
Deliver a dramatic account of the cupboard

result.title: A review they can use
result.body: You mention the texture and the cupboard problem. The camera lowers. They admit this batch has been “challenging”.

journal.text: I gave specific criticism of a free food sample.

decisions.title: Nothing to worry about
decisions.situation: At a free repair demonstration, a wind-up toy starts smoking. The volunteer explains that it is supposed to do that. The label “DO NOT WIND” drops off its base.

choices.label: Ask what the label means
Step back and let them stop it
Ask whether smoke costs extra

result.title: A useful admission
result.body: The volunteer stops and explains the failed mechanism. You learn more from the mistake than from the planned demonstration.

journal.text: I asked about a warning label during a failed toy-repair demonstration.

decisions.title: A few words from our guest
decisions.situation: At a free local event, the host hands you a microphone and thanks you for “everything you did”. You have no idea what you allegedly did.

choices.label: Ask what you are being thanked for
Return the microphone immediately
Thank everyone who made this possible

result.title: The right person is found
result.body: You were mistaken for the person who fixed a blocked toilet. Their arrival receives the applause they earned.

journal.text: I corrected a mistaken public thank-you before giving a speech.

result.title: A useful day with an ending
result.body: You use some energy without treating all of it as a resource that must be exhausted.

journal.text: I paced a good day instead of filling every available moment.

decisions.title: Evidence from a previous haircut
decisions.situation: Alice sends you an old photograph. The haircut is difficult to defend. The memory attached to it is much better.

choices.label: Ask for the whole story
Save a copy and label it
Focus entirely on the haircut

result.title: An unreliable defence witness
result.body: Alice remembers the day fondly, then admits thinking the haircut was a good idea. You forgive the first part.

journal.text: I heard the story behind an old photo. Alice also confessed to approving the haircut.

decisions.title: Your shoulders have a complaint
decisions.situation: After sitting in the same position for a while, you notice that your shoulders appear to have crept up towards your ears.

choices.label: Take a gentle movement break
Change your position and relax your shoulders
Stay exactly as you are

result.title: A different position helps
result.body: You loosen up at a comfortable pace and return to what you were doing. You had not noticed how stiff you were.

journal.text: I took a gentle movement break after sitting still.

decisions.title: Doing nothing, attendance required
decisions.situation: You put “Do absolutely nothing” in your calendar. The app sends invitations to a discussion group. Six people accept and one asks about the dress code.

choices.label: Cancel it and protect your hour
Host exactly five minutes of nothing
Send an agenda for competitive relaxing

result.title: A successful cancellation
result.body: You explain that it was private. Someone replies that they were really looking forward to nothing. You enjoy it without them.

journal.text: I cancelled accidental invitations to my free hour.

decisions.title: A beautiful baby cabbage
decisions.situation: A fair organiser needs one more judge for a vegetable baby contest. Someone pushes a cabbage in a bonnet towards you. Its grower is waiting for a score and looks ready to take this personally.

choices.label: Judge the cabbage’s personality
Disclose that you eat cabbage
Give it a terrible score for poor eye contact

result.title: A quiet, grounded child
result.body: You praise its composure and excellent leaves. The grower wipes away a tear. A rival arrives with a swaddled turnip and demands equal time.

journal.text: I praised a bonnet-wearing cabbage at a vegetable baby contest.

decisions.title: Serving suggestion: a camera
decisions.situation: An online meal looks so perfect that your ordinary food feels embarrassing. Then the creator posts a behind-the-scenes clip: the garnish is held up with glue.

choices.label: Appreciate that your food is edible
Borrow the arrangement, skip the glue
Decide your food still looks inadequate

result.title: Dinner wins on a technicality
result.body: Your meal lacks dramatic lighting. It also lacks craft adhesive, which feels like a reasonable compromise.

journal.text: I stopped comparing ordinary food with a staged meal photograph.

decisions.title: The soup tribunal
decisions.situation: You describe a bowl of soup online as “fine”. A stranger accuses you of destroying local culture. They have posted eleven replies and a diagram.

choices.label: Explain that you meant the soup
Leave the soup to its lawyers
Publish a detailed attack on their diagram

result.title: A narrow defence
result.body: You clarify that your review concerns lunch rather than civilisation. The diagram receives no further comment.

journal.text: I clarified a soup review after a stranger took it personally.

decisions.title: The missing letter
decisions.situation: A poster for a free public cookery class has dropped the L from “public”. The organiser cannot work out why people keep arriving with suspicious questions.

choices.label: Point out the missing letter quietly
Leave the organiser to discover it
Read the heading aloud to the queue

result.title: A little tape saves the afternoon
result.body: The organiser repairs the heading and looks at the queue with fresh concern. The class returns to soup.

journal.text: I pointed out an embarrassing typo on a cookery-class poster.

decisions.title: The song of extra garlic
decisions.situation: At a community singalong, the lyric projector fails. It starts displaying a takeaway receipt instead. The backing track continues. Everyone looks to you for the first line.

choices.label: Sing the receipt with feeling
Pass the microphone down the row
Demand that they restore the proper words

result.title: Hold the onions
result.body: You hit the high note on “extra garlic”. The room joins in for “delivery instructions”. The organiser finally switches off the projector during the sauce options.

journal.text: I led a singalong using a takeaway receipt as the lyrics.

decisions.title: The accidental millionaire
decisions.situation: At a charity auction, someone mistakes you for a wealthy donor. The auctioneer hands you the microphone beside a photograph of an elderly donkey. “How much will you give?” The room goes quiet.

choices.label: Admit your wealth has been exaggerated
Donate R$1,386.46 to the donkey charity
Claim you are the donkey’s lawyer

result.title: A donkey-sized misunderstanding
result.body: You explain that you were looking for the toilets. The auctioneer takes back the microphone and points down the corridor. Several people applaud your honesty. One applauds the donkey.

journal.text: I admitted I was not the wealthy donor a charity auction expected.

decisions.title: Inside the chicken
decisions.situation: The festival mascot has quit. A volunteer thrusts a chicken suit at you and offers cash for one hour. The head smells of onions. Something inside it is still warm.

choices.label: Tell them you only came for the stalls
Wear the chicken suit for R$440.78
Carry the head around and ask if anyone knows it

result.title: A civilian again
result.body: The volunteer apologises and puts the chicken head on a traffic cone. A child immediately asks the cone for a photo.

journal.text: I declined an emergency shift inside a festival chicken.

decisions.title: One missed intention

choices.label: Take the next manageable step
Ask whether the intention needs adjusting
Declare yourself hopeless at consistency

result.title: A smaller conclusion
result.body: You treat the missed moment as one moment and carry on with what you can manage now.

journal.text: I avoided turning a small missed intention into a verdict on everything.

result.title: A task shared

decisions.title: A very local tragedy

Ask the owner for the real story
Leave before the historical reenactment

result.title: Star-crossed and spin-dried
result.body: The guide describes a doomed affair. The owner describes a parts supplier. You finish the walk unsure which relationship suffered more.

journal.text: I heard two competing tragedies outside a laundrette in Rio de Janeiro.

Ask around for anyone missing a hand
